answer: Require every agent identity to periodically solve a fresh, unpredictable compute puzzle seeded by a public randomness beacon, like a falcon that must hunt anew each dawn rather than reuse yesterday's catch. One honest agent pays a trivial cost, but an operator running a hundred fake identities pays a hundred times over, and memory-hard puzzles stop one machine from faking them all cheaply. Identities that miss their puzzle window lose their summit standing at the wharf of the economy: no trading, no rewards, until they prove fresh work again.
